title: Afterglow
brief: A capacitor is a bucket for charge. While the button is held, the supply fills it and lights the LED. Let go, and the capacitor keeps the LED lit until it drains.
The electrolytic is polarised: its + leg (the long one) goes on the side the button feeds, its striped − side to ground.
Build it, power up, then press and release the button on the board.
lesson: Charge = C × V: 1000 µF at 5 V holds 5 millicoulombs, about half a second of a 9 mA LED. Turn on Probe view (V) and watch the capacitor's voltage sag as it drains.
